headline: Van Hollen wants Schumer's job. Schumer: I have the votes.
summary: Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said Thursday he will challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader when Democrats take the chamber in January. Schumer has led Senate Democrats since 2017 and says he has the votes. Van Hollen calls himself the underdog and counts more than 10 senators on his side. The secret ballot is December 1.

cover_question.q: Why dump the guy who won?

cover_answer: Van Hollen: voters want change. Schumer: I have the votes.
table_question: If your team just won, is that the time to change the captain?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: In the Senate, one big group of lawmakers picks a leader, like a team picking a captain. The captain now is Chuck Schumer, and on Thursday a senator named Chris Van Hollen said he wants the job. In three weeks the team votes in secret. Nothing changes for you either way.
5-7.why: A captain's vote is a thing they have seen. The names stay light.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, and the Senate is not. A team picking a captain is, so the script runs on that and keeps the two names as names. The secret vote in three weeks is the one fact to hold. Expect "who will win?" Schumer says he has the votes, and nobody will know until December 1.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Democrats won the Senate, so in January their leader runs it. Chuck Schumer has led them since 2017 and wants to keep the job. Chris Van Hollen says voters asked for change and he should lead instead. Senators vote in secret on December 1: a class picking a captain, heads down, hands up.
8-12.why: A win, a job, a challenger, a secret vote: the chain in order.
8-12.why_long: At ten they are working through cause and effect and fairness: Democrats won, so their leader runs the Senate, so the job is worth a fight. The secret ballot is the mechanism, and heads-down voting in a classroom is the same thing. Expect "why is it secret?" So no senator has to say in public which colleague they picked.

13-17.script: Your team just won. Replace the captain? Chris Van Hollen says voters called for change and Chuck Schumer, leader since 2017, should go. Schumer says he has the votes. Second: Van Hollen admits he's the underdog. Is a race you expect to lose still worth running?
13-17.why: Mandate or momentum: they can argue it from both ends.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: Democrats won under Schumer, and the voters may have wanted somebody new. The script asks whether a win is a mandate for the leader or for change, and whether a race you expect to lose is worth running. Expect "who will win?" The report names nine public backers for Schumer, one for Van Hollen.

5-7.q: Who's the boss of the Senate?
5-7.a: Chuck Schumer leads the Democrats there. Three weeks till they vote on it.

8-12.a: So no senator has to say out loud which colleague they picked.
Axios names nine senators for Schumer. Van Hollen claims more than 10.

13-17.q: Why dump the guy who won?
13-17.a: Voters want change, he says. Progressives: Schumer didn't fight.
Underdog, he says, with 10-plus senators. Schumer says he has the votes.
